Lessons.Title: Features of Trigonometric Graphs (Part 1)
ExplanationParagraphs: Source-aligned goals: Identify the midline, amplitude, and horizontal translation in trigonometric functions presented graphically and with equations. Predict how changing the value of $k$ in $y=cos(kx)$ changes the graph of the function for whole number values of $k$.
For y=cos(kx) with k nonzero, one full cycle occurs when kx advances 2π, so period is 2π/|k|. Horizontal shifts and reflections do not alter absolute period.

Practice Problem 2: Select all the functions that have period \(\pi\). \(y = \cos\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)\) \(y = \sin\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)\) Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 3: Sketch a graph of \(a(\theta) = \cos(3\theta)\). Compare the graph of \(a\) to the graph of \(b(\theta)=\cos(\theta)\). How are the two graphs alike? How are they different? Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
